Есть гипотеза: в жизни каждого самозанятого в Великобритании есть хотя бы одна конкретная повторяющаяся задача, которую все ненавидят и которую никто нормально не решил. SurveyPage.confidentiality: Ваши ответы строго конфиденциальны. Они поступают напрямую в закрытую базу данных — никаких третьих сторон, никаких маркетинговых списков, никакой передачи. Читаю только я.

q1_admin_task.label: Какая рутинная задача последний раз отняла у вас больше времени, чем должна была?

q2_currently_paying.label: За какие инструменты, сервисы или услуги вы сейчас платите, чтобы бизнес работал?

meta.title: Privacy notice — Sole Trader Discovery
meta.description: How I collect, store and use the answers you share through the discovery survey.

sections.heading: Who runs this
sections.body: This research project is operated by Dmytro Fenko (publishing as Dmitry Fenko), a UK sole trader trading as Fenko Team. I’m the data controller for everything described below. The project doesn’t meet the conditions in UK GDPR Article 37 that require a Data Protection Officer, so I haven’t appointed one — I handle every data protection matter personally. If you need to reach me about your data, write to support@fenko.dev and I’ll reply personally.

sections.heading: ICO registration
sections.body: I’m registered with the UK Information Commissioner’s Office as a data controller and pay the annual data protection fee. My ICO registration number is ZC141876. You can verify it on the public register at ico.org.uk/ESDWebPages/Search.

sections.heading: What I collect
sections.body: Only what you type into the survey: your email address, a short description of your business, how long you’ve been running it, your free-text answers to three open-ended questions, and a server-stamped timestamp recording when you ticked the consent box and which version of this notice was in force at that moment. All of it is collected directly from you when you submit the form; nothing is bought, scraped, or inferred from other sources. I don’t use analytics, cookies, fingerprinting, or session recording, and there’s no tracking script on this site. Providing this information is entirely voluntary — there’s no contract or legal obligation to participate. If you’d rather not, just don’t submit the survey.

sections.heading: Why I collect it
sections.body: To understand whether there’s a useful product to build for UK sole traders, and to contact you if I do build one. That’s the entire purpose. Your email won’t be sold, shared, or used for marketing of unrelated products.

sections.heading: Where it’s stored
sections.body: Your responses are stored in a Supabase Postgres database hosted in the EU (Frankfurt), encrypted at rest by the platform and transmitted over TLS. Supabase Inc. — the company behind the platform — is incorporated in the United States, so the transfer to them is covered by the standard contractual clauses and the UK International Data Transfer Agreement (IDTA) included in Supabase’s published Data Processing Agreement (supabase.com/legal/dpa), which provide appropriate safeguards under UK GDPR Article 46. The website is served by Vercel Inc. (US), and the serverless function that receives and validates your form submission is configured to run in Vercel’s Frankfurt region (eu-central) — so the form data is processed inside the EU before it reaches the database. Vercel publishes a Data Processing Agreement at vercel.com/legal/dpa that incorporates the standard contractual clauses and the UK IDTA as transfer mechanisms. Both Supabase’s and Vercel’s DPAs apply to this project through incorporation by reference in their standard terms — they have not been separately countersigned. Vercel also collects standard request metadata (IP address, User-Agent, URL, timestamp) in its edge and runtime logs as part of CDN operation — these logs are retained for up to 24 hours on the current plan and are accessible to me through the Vercel dashboard. Vercel acts as our processor under their DPA. If a server-side validation error occurs while you submit the form, a small fragment of your submitted answer (up to about 1,000 characters) may also transiently appear in Vercel’s function logs for the same retention window before being auto-deleted; these logs are accessible only to me. Beyond the platform staff at Supabase and Vercel (who have administrative access to their infrastructure under their respective DPAs), I’m the only person who reads and analyses the data.

sections.heading: Analytics
sections.body: I use Vercel Web Analytics to count anonymous page views and understand which posts drive visits. The service generates a server-side hash from each visitor’s IP address and User-Agent (rotated every 24 hours) and records: the page route visited, the country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2), the device type, browser, and operating system. The hash cannot be reversed to your IP and is not linked across days, sessions, or other websites. Nothing is stored on your device — no cookies, no localStorage, no fingerprinting beyond the daily server-side hash. The lawful basis for this processing is legitimate interests under UK GDPR Article 6(1)(f): I need basic page-level signal to understand which discovery posts reach the right audience, and the data collected is minimal, anonymous, and proportionate. You have an absolute right to object to this processing under Article 21 — email support@fenko.dev with the subject line “opt-out analytics” and I’ll exclude your future visits.

sections.heading: Performance Insights
sections.body: Alongside Vercel Web Analytics, I use Vercel Speed Insights to measure how the site performs in real browsers — Core Web Vitals such as Largest Contentful Paint, Cumulative Layout Shift, and Interaction to Next Paint. Each measurement records: the page route, the country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2), the device type, browser, operating system, and the metric value. By Vercel's design, the data is anonymous and is not associated with any individual visitor or IP address — measurements cannot be tied back to you. Nothing is stored on your device. The lawful basis for this processing is legitimate interests under UK GDPR Article 6(1)(f): I need real-user performance data to detect regressions and prioritise fixes that affect actual visitors, and the data collected is minimal, anonymous, and proportionate. The right to object under Article 21 applies on the same terms as analytics — email support@fenko.dev with the subject line “opt-out analytics” and I’ll exclude your future visits from both.

sections.heading: How long I keep it
sections.body: I keep your responses for as long as the project is active, plus up to 12 months after, to allow follow-up analysis and any final write-up of findings. After that, or whenever you ask, I delete your record permanently.

sections.heading: Your rights (UK GDPR)
sections.body: Under UK GDPR you have the right to: access a copy of your data; correct anything inaccurate; have your data deleted; restrict how I use it; receive your data in a portable format (e.g. a CSV); object to processing; and withdraw your consent at any time. To exercise any of these, email support@fenko.dev. I’ll respond within one month — usually much faster.

sections.heading: Lawful basis
sections.body: Consent. By ticking the box on the final step of the survey, you agree to this notice. You can withdraw consent at any time by emailing me — that triggers deletion.

sections.heading: What I don’t do
sections.body: I don’t sell data. I don’t share it with third parties beyond Supabase (the database host) and Vercel (the website host). I don’t use it to train AI models. I don’t run ads. I don’t have a marketing funnel. There’s also no automated decision-making or profiling — no algorithm makes any decision about you based on your answers.

sections.heading: Complaints
sections.body: If you think I’ve handled your data unlawfully, you have the right to lodge a complaint with the UK’s data protection regulator — the Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO). You can reach them at ico.org.uk or 0303 123 1113. I’d appreciate the chance to fix things first if you email me, but you’re not obliged to.

meta.title: Cookie notice — Sole Trader Discovery
meta.description: This site sets one cookie: NEXT_LOCALE, which remembers your chosen language. No analytics, no tracking, no fingerprinting.

CookiesPage.label: Cookie notice
CookiesPage.headline: One cookie. No tracking. Nothing else.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body: This website sets one cookie: NEXT_LOCALE, which stores the language you've chosen (English, Russian, or Ukrainian) so the site can remember your choice on your next visit. That's the only cookie. We also use Vercel Web Analytics, which generates an anonymous server-side fingerprint hash for each visit - nothing is stored on your device, and visitors cannot be tracked across days, sessions, or sites. Other than NEXT_LOCALE, no information is stored in your browser. There's no third-party tracking, no advertising, no profiling. No third-party scripts of any kind. Nothing is stored in localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, the Cache API, or any other client-side storage technology.

sections.heading: What cookies are
sections.body: Cookies are small text files that a website stores in your browser to remember information about you — your preferences, session state, or behaviour across pages and visits. Many sites use them for analytics, advertising, login sessions, and A/B testing. This site does none of those things. The only cookie it sets is NEXT_LOCALE, which stores a single value: the language code you selected.

sections.heading: What this site actually does
sections.body: When you click the language switcher in the header, the site sets a NEXT_LOCALE cookie containing one of three values: 'en', 'ru', or 'uk'. The cookie is read on subsequent visits to remember your preference and show the site in your chosen language. Under the Privacy and Electronic Communications Regulations 2003 (regulation 6), this is permitted without prior consent because it is strictly necessary to provide the language preference you explicitly requested. The cookie has no other purpose, contains no personal data beyond the locale code, and is not shared with anyone. When you submit the survey, your answers are sent directly to a database (Supabase, hosted in the EU). That request does not involve any additional cookies. Vercel Web Analytics, which is enabled on this site, generates a server-side fingerprint hash from your IP address and User-Agent (rotated every 24 hours) to count anonymous page views — it does not store anything on your device, does not link visits across days or sites, and does not use cookies or any other client-side storage. Vercel Speed Insights is also enabled and measures Core Web Vitals (loading time, interactivity, layout stability) using native browser APIs; the readings are sent to Vercel anonymously, are not associated with any visitor or IP address, and likewise do not store anything on your device. Beyond NEXT_LOCALE, your browser does not store anything locally from this site — no other cookies, no localStorage entries, no IndexedDB databases, no service worker caches. There is no session token, no persistent identifier, and no tracking pixel.

sections.heading: If that ever changes
sections.body: If I ever add anything beyond NEXT_LOCALE — for example, analytics or A/B testing — I will update this notice first, implement a proper consent mechanism, and tell you clearly what is being used and why. Until then, NEXT_LOCALE is the only cookie this site sets.

sections.heading: Contact
sections.body: If you have questions about this or notice something that looks like tracking behaviour, please email support@fenko.dev.
